title: Rabbi Shimon Dima or Dayyana

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Peah, beginning of chapter 6: Rabbi Shimon Dima taught before Rabbi Ze’ira. In Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim, chapter 4, halakhah 10, the reading is Rabbi Shimon Dayyana.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The Guggenheimer digital texts of Jerusalem Talmud Peah 6:1 and Nedarim 4:10 have Shimon Dima and Shimon Dayyana respectively, both reciting before Rabbi Zeira. Dayyana means “the judge”; Dima is left unsegmented rather than asserting “of the sea.” The supplied בירושלטי/קוטי/פ״ר/הנרםא are read contextually as בירושלמי/קומי/פ״ד/הגרסא, supported by these passages, not by printed pixels.

The whole selected Guggenheimer passages in Jerusalem Talmud Peah 6:1 and Nedarim 4:10 support the two forms and the direction “before Rabbi Zeira.” The contextual readings of the damaged supplied words remain translation readings, without canonical Hebrew repair or printed-page verification.
